name: Graph and Temporal Memory
question: Can the agent remember who is linked to what, and since when?
summary: Stores memory as entities and relationships with time on every edge: who holds which account, who is nominee, which address was valid from when to when. New facts that contradict old ones close the old edge with an end date instead of deleting it, so the agent answers from what is true now and can still explain what was true then. Multi-hop questions follow edges, which plain vector memory struggles to do.
useCases: Customer relationships that change: nominees, addresses, authorised signatories
Questions that chain facts: “the nominee on the account opened after the move”
Audit needs: what did we know, and when

items.detail: typed edges such as holder_of, nominee_of, lives_at
when the fact was true in the world
contradicted edges get an end date
graph traversal plus text and vector search

steps: Extract entities and relationships from each conversation or note
Attach valid-from and valid-to times, and when the fact was recorded
Close contradicted edges instead of deleting them
Answer by traversing the graph for the current time, with vector search for fuzzy matches
pitfalls: Deleting old facts and losing the audit trail
Keeping contradictory facts with no dates, so answers flip
Extraction errors creating wrong edges that nobody reviews
remember: Link the facts, date the links, close old ones.
caption: Illustrative: Kaveri Bank, a fictional bank, gives relationship managers memory across three years of customer notes.

steps.title: Store episodes, extract a graph
steps.text: Each note or conversation is added as an episode. The library extracts entities (Priya, account 4471, Rahul, Sunita) and the relationships between them.

steps.title: Record when each fact became true
steps.text: The reference time says when the note applies. Every edge gets a valid-from time, and the system also records when it learned the fact.

steps.title: Close contradicted facts
steps.text: The new nominee contradicts “Rahul is nominee”, so that edge gets an end date. Nothing is deleted, so you can still say who was nominee in 2024.

steps.title: Search the graph for the current state
steps.text: A question is answered by searching edges and text together, preferring facts that are valid now.

steps.title: Show when the answer was true
steps.text: The answer carries its validity: Sunita, nominee since 10 June 2025. A relationship manager can see the history.

steps.title: Test multi-hop questions
steps.text: Measure on questions that chain facts, such as “the nominee on the account opened after the address change”. Here accuracy rises from 45% to 85%.

practice.scenario: Kaveri Bank, a fictional bank, gives relationship managers an assistant that remembers three years of customer notes. Each note becomes an episode in a temporal knowledge graph: customers, accounts, nominees and addresses are linked, every link has a valid-from date, and a change such as a new nominee closes the old link with an end date. The assistant answers from what is true now and can show the history.

industries.use: Nominees, joint holders and signatories that change over time
Policyholders, dependants and addresses across renewals
Care relationships and consents with start and end dates

practice.analogy: A family tree with dates on every line, drawn in pencil: when something changes you add the end date, you do not rub the line out.

library.name: Graphiti
library.what: Open-source temporal knowledge graph from Zep: episodes in, entities and dated edges out, with hybrid search.

practice.note: Needs a running Neo4j and an LLM API key for extraction. Method names may change between versions.

samples.code:
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from graphiti_core import Graphiti
from graphiti_core.nodes import EpisodeType

async def main():
    graph = Graphiti("bolt://localhost:7687", "neo4j", "password")
    await graph.build_indices_and_constraints()
    for when, text in [
        (datetime(2024, 3, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc), "Priya made Rahul nominee on account 4471."),
        (datetime(2025, 6, 10, tzinfo=timezone.utc), "Priya changed the nominee on account 4471 to Sunita."),
    ]:
        await graph.add_episode(name=f"note-{when.date()}", episode_body=text,
                                source=EpisodeType.text, source_description="RM note",
                                reference_time=when)
    for edge in await graph.search("Who is the nominee on account 4471?"):
        print(edge.fact, edge.valid_at, edge.invalid_at)
    await graph.close()

asyncio.run(main())

interview.question: When would you use a temporal knowledge graph for agent memory?
interview.answer: When facts relate to each other and change over time, such as nominees, addresses and account holders, and when questions chain facts or ask what was true at a date. Close old edges with end dates rather than deleting.

interview.question: What is the difference between valid time and recorded time?
interview.answer: Valid time is when a fact was true in the world; recorded time is when the system learned it. Keeping both lets you answer what was true then and what we knew then.

mistakes.fix: Close them with an end date

mistakes.mistake: Using vector memory for chained questions
